newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cr Lyonnais says Eurotunnel provisions adequate.
newsitem.headline: Cr Lyonnais says Eurotunnel provisions adequate.

text.p: French state-controlled bank Credit Lyonnais, one of the biggest lenders to Eurotunnel, said on Thursday its provisions against exposure to the debt-laden Anglo-French channel tunnel operator were sufficient and it had no plans to increase them.

"Our provisioning seems to me to be adequate," bank chairman Jean Peyrelevade told a news conference after reporting that Credit Lyonnais's first-half profit rose to 67 million francs ($12.93 million) from 36 million francs a year earlier.
Credit Lyonnais was reported last year to have 2.35 billion francs in total loans to Eurotunnel, including 2.09 billion in junior debt.
The bank made a provision in its accounts last year for its Eurotunnel exposure but did not reveal the size nor say how much of its total loan had been classed as a likely loss.

Peyrelvade praised the last-minute deal reached this week aimed at rescheduling Eurotunnel's 70 billion franc debt mountain. The agreement averted the threat of Eurotunnel being pushed into administration under French law.
"I have no doubt it will be positive for shareholders and for bankers," he said.
Peyrelevade said the banks had made concessions to reach an agreement which was in the "general interest."

Had the bankers pushed the Channel tunnel operator into liquidation, the bankers could have been mired in "(legal) procedures, conflicts, disputes" that would have taken a long time to resolve, he said. ($1=5.183 French Franc)
